p1: [low, ominous] In twenty seventeen, scientists dug up a serial killer's grave... [whispers] to prove he was really in it.
[low] For over a century, people said he'd escaped the hangman.
[low, ominous] His name was H. H. Holmes.
[low] In eighteen ninety-three, near Chicago's World's Fair, he built a three-story building.
[low] Newspapers called it... [low, ominous] the Murder Castle. Trapdoors. Secret rooms. A chute to the basement.
[low] Historians say most of that... [whispers] was never proven.
[low] He confessed to twenty-seven murders... [low, tense] but some of his victims were still alive.
[low] Historians can confirm... [low, ominous] about nine.
[low] In eighteen ninety-six, he was hanged.
[low] So in twenty seventeen, they dug ten feet down... [low, tense] and hit cement.
[low] He'd asked for that himself. [whispers] So no one could ever dig him up.
[low] His clothes were preserved... [whispers] and his mustache was still there.
[low] His teeth matched. It was him. [low, ominous] How many he really killed... [whispers] no one will ever know.
